# ClaimsDesk Modernization - RFP Extract and Discovery Notes

## 1. Background

Meridian Assurance Group is a regional property and casualty insurer operating in Washington, Oregon and Idaho.
We write personal auto, homeowners and small commercial policies through a network of 340 independent agents.
Our claims organisation processes approximately 58,000 first-notice-of-loss events per year.
The current claims intake and adjudication system, internally called ClaimsDesk, was built in 2011 on .NET Framework 4.8 with an Oracle 19c database.
ClaimsDesk is reaching end of vendor support and cannot be hosted on any current-generation Windows Server release.
We issued this RFP to select a partner to design and deliver a modernised claims portal on a supported, cloud-native stack.

## 2. Current Systems Landscape

Guidewire ClaimCenter is used by our claims examiners for reserve setting and payment authorisation; ClaimsDesk must continue to exchange claim status and payment data with it.
SAP S/4HANA is our finance and general-ledger system of record; every approved claim payment must post to SAP as a journal entry.
Okta is our corporate identity provider and already issues SSO for 1,850 internal staff across claims, underwriting and finance.
Adjusters currently rediscover claim details by re-keying data between ClaimsDesk and Guidewire ClaimCenter, which our claims VP flagged as the single biggest source of processing delay.
The existing ClaimsDesk database holds nineteen years of claim history, roughly 4.2 TB of structured data plus 1.1 TB of scanned PDF and image attachments.
A separate legacy mainframe, referred to internally as the Policy Admin System, is being retired by a different program and is out of scope for this engagement.

## 3. Business Requirements

BR1. The solution must reduce average claim-intake processing time from 45 minutes to under 15 minutes per first-notice-of-loss.
BR2. The solution must give claims examiners a single screen that shows policy, claim and payment status without switching between ClaimsDesk and Guidewire ClaimCenter.
BR3. The solution should improve first-contact resolution for straightforward auto glass and windshield claims to reduce reliance on phone-based adjusters.
BR4. The solution must support our 340 independent agents submitting new claims directly rather than calling our call centre.
BR5. The solution could introduce a policyholder-facing status tracker so claimants can check progress without calling an examiner.

## 4. Functional Requirements

FR1. Claims examiners must be able to create, update and close a claim record, including reserve amounts synchronised from Guidewire ClaimCenter.
FR2. The portal must let agents upload first-notice-of-loss documents, including photos, estimates and police reports, directly against a claim.
FR3. The portal must display a consolidated claim timeline combining ClaimsDesk activity, Guidewire ClaimCenter reserve changes and SAP S/4HANA payment postings.
FR4. Claims examiners must be able to approve a payment that then posts automatically to SAP S/4HANA as a journal entry without manual re-entry.
FR5. The portal should let policyholders view claim status, upload additional documents and message their assigned adjuster.
FR6. Supervisors must be able to reassign claims between examiners and view team workload dashboards.
FR7. The portal must retain full claim history for at least seven years to satisfy state insurance record-keeping rules.
FR8. The portal should allow examiners to flag a claim for special-investigation-unit review, notifying the SIU team automatically.
FR9. Independent agents must be able to see the status of claims they submitted but must not see claims submitted by other agencies.
FR10. The portal could offer examiners a suggested reserve range based on similar historical claims, clearly marked as advisory only.

## 5. Non-Functional Requirements

NFR1. The portal must be available 99.9% of the time during business hours, 7am to 9pm Pacific, Monday through Saturday.
NFR2. Claim search results must return within 2 seconds for 95% of queries under normal load.
NFR3. The system must support 1,850 internal staff and approximately 240,000 active policyholders as registered users.
NFR4. The portal must support at least 900 concurrent internal sessions during a regional catastrophe event without degradation.
NFR5. Recovery point objective for claim data must be under 15 minutes and recovery time objective must be under 4 hours.
NFR6. The portal must be accessible to WCAG 2.1 AA standards because several of our agent partners have accessibility requirements on staff.
NFR7. All claim and payment activity must be captured in an immutable audit log retained for a minimum of seven years.

## 6. Integration Requirements

INT1. The portal must integrate with Guidewire ClaimCenter for reserve and payment-authorisation data, in near real time.
INT2. The portal must integrate with SAP S/4HANA to post approved claim payments as finance journal entries.
INT3. The portal must federate authentication through Okta using SAML or OIDC for all internal staff.
INT4. The portal should integrate with our document-imaging vendor, currently Hyland OnBase, to retrieve scanned historical claim files.
INT5. The portal must expose a secure API for the 340 independent agents' agency-management systems to submit first-notice-of-loss data.
INT6. The portal should send SMS and email notifications through our existing Twilio account when a claim status changes.

## 7. Data Requirements

DATA1. Claim, policy and payment data must be migrated from the legacy ClaimsDesk Oracle 19c database with full referential integrity.
DATA2. The 1.1 TB of scanned attachments must be migrated or linked without loss of the original document metadata.
DATA3. Claim and policyholder data is personally identifiable information and must be classified and handled accordingly.
DATA4. Historical claim data older than seven years may be archived to cold storage rather than kept in the primary database.
DATA5. Data quality checks must confirm that migrated claim totals reconcile exactly against the legacy ClaimsDesk reporting extracts before cutover.

## 8. Security and Compliance

SEC1. The solution must comply with the EU General Data Protection Regulation for the subset of policyholders who are EU residents on international travel riders.
SEC2. All personal data must be encrypted at rest and in transit using current industry-standard algorithms.
SEC3. Role-based access control must ensure examiners only see claims assigned to their team, with supervisor override logged.
SEC4. Multi-factor authentication must be enforced for all internal staff accessing claim payment approval functions.
SEC5. The solution must undergo a third-party penetration test before go-live and annually thereafter.
SEC6. Independent agents accessing the agent API must be issued scoped API credentials that can be revoked individually.

## 9. Technology Preferences

TECH1. Our infrastructure team standardised on Microsoft Azure two years ago and we would prefer the new claims portal to run on Azure.
TECH2. We are open to a managed PostgreSQL or Azure SQL database as the system of record, replacing the Oracle 19c instance.
TECH3. Our internal engineering team has React and .NET experience, so a stack that our staff can support after handover is preferred.

## 10. Delivery Constraints and Timeline

CON1. The new portal must go live before our June 2027 policy renewal season begins, which the program office has translated into a target of 46 weeks from contract signature.
CON2. Legacy ClaimsDesk must keep running in parallel with the new portal for a 60-day stabilisation period after cutover.
CON3. Our claims operations team can dedicate at most two business analysts and one QA lead to this program part-time; the delivery partner is expected to staff the rest.
CON4. A pilot rollout to the Idaho claims team is required before statewide rollout to Washington and Oregon.

## 11. Discovery Call Notes - 2026-08-21

Attendees: VP Claims Operations, IT Director, Enterprise Architect (Meridian); Engagement Manager, Solution Architect (delivery partner).
The VP Claims Operations reiterated that re-keying data between ClaimsDesk and Guidewire ClaimCenter is the top complaint from examiners in engagement surveys.
The IT Director confirmed Okta is the corporate standard and no other identity provider will be considered.
The Enterprise Architect flagged that the Hyland OnBase contract renews in November 2026 and asked whether the new portal could eventually replace it, but this is explicitly out of scope for this phase.
The IT Director could not yet confirm whether SAP S/4HANA exposes a REST API or only IDoc/BAPI interfaces for journal posting and will follow up after checking with the SAP basis team.
No decision has been made yet on whether the policyholder-facing status tracker (FR5) ships in the initial release or a fast-follow phase.

statements.text: Meridian Assurance Group needs its legacy .NET/Oracle ClaimsDesk portal replaced with a cloud-native claims platform on Azure, integrated with Guidewire ClaimCenter, SAP S/4HANA and Okta, serving roughly 242,000 internal and policyholder users within a 46-week window; the SAP integration pattern and the phasing of the policyholder status tracker remain open.
statements.label: ai-interpretation

statements.text: ClaimsDesk Modernization Program serves 5 business objectives set by Meridian Assurance Group (BR_01, BR_02, BR_03, BR_04 and BR_05); each is detailed under Business objectives.
statements.label: customer-requested

statements.text: The solution is organised into 6 capability areas (Application Experience, Platform Foundation, Data Platform, Systems Integration, AI Capabilities and Security and Compliance) and connects to Guidewire ClaimCenter (SYS_01), SAP S/4HANA (SYS_02), Okta (SYS_03) and Hyland OnBase (SYS_05).
statements.label: ai-interpretation

statements.text: Today Meridian Assurance Group relies on Legacy ClaimsDesk Portal: The current claims intake and adjudication system, built in 2011 on .NET Framework 4.8 with an Oracle 19c database, being replaced by this program.
statements.label: customer-requested

statements.text: Until this is addressed, Meridian Assurance Group cannot achieve "Reduce claim-intake processing time" (BR_01), "Unified claim, policy and payment view for examiners" (BR_02), "Improve first-contact resolution for simple claims" (BR_03), "Enable direct agent claim submission" (BR_04) and "Policyholder claim-status tracker (candidate)" (BR_05).
statements.label: customer-requested

statements.text: BR_01 - Reduce claim-intake processing time: Reduce average claim-intake processing time from 45 minutes to under 15 minutes per first-notice-of-loss event.
statements.label: customer-requested

statements.text: BR_02 - Unified claim, policy and payment view for examiners: Give claims examiners a single screen showing policy, claim and payment status without switching between ClaimsDesk and Guidewire ClaimCenter.

statements.text: BR_03 - Improve first-contact resolution for simple claims: Improve first-contact resolution for straightforward auto glass and windshield claims, reducing reliance on phone-based adjusters.
statements.label: customer-requested

statements.text: BR_04 - Enable direct agent claim submission: Support the 340 independent agents submitting new claims directly rather than routing through the call centre.
statements.label: customer-requested

statements.text: BR_05 - Policyholder claim-status tracker (candidate): Introduce a policyholder-facing status tracker so claimants can check progress without calling an examiner.

journeys.name: Claims Examiner journey
steps: Step 1: Claims examiners create, update and close a claim record, including reserve amounts synchronised from Guidewire ClaimCenter (FR_01; delivered by CAP_08).
Step 2: Claims examiners approve a payment that posts automatically to SAP S/4HANA as a journal entry without manual re-entry (FR_04; delivered by CAP_05).
Step 3: Let examiners flag a claim for special-investigation-unit review, notifying the SIU team automatically (FR_09; delivered by CAP_04).
Step 4: Offer examiners a suggested reserve range based on similar historical claims, clearly marked as advisory only (FR_10; delivered by CAP_19).

journeys.name: Independent Agent journey
steps: Step 1: Agents upload first-notice-of-loss documents, including photos, estimates and police reports, directly against a claim (FR_02; delivered by CAP_02).
Step 2: Independent agents see the status of claims they submitted but never see claims submitted by other agencies (FR_07; delivered by CAP_03).

journeys.name: Policyholder journey
steps: Step 1: Policyholders view claim status, upload additional documents and message their assigned adjuster (FR_05; delivered by CAP_06).

journeys.name: Claims Supervisor journey
steps: Step 1: Supervisors reassign claims between examiners and view team workload dashboards (FR_06; delivered by CAP_01).

capabilities.name: Dashboards and Reporting
capabilities.scope: Provide dashboards and reporting so stakeholders can monitor operational and business metrics without manual data extraction. It delivers: FR_06 (Supervisor reassignment and workload view).
capabilities.label: customer-requested
acceptance: A named stakeholder dashboard loads the current metrics without a manual export step.
Report figures reconcile with the underlying transactional data for a sample period.

capabilities.name: Document Management
capabilities.scope: Provide document management covering upload, storage, retrieval and lifecycle control for the files the solution manages. It delivers: FR_02 (First-notice-of-loss document upload). It connects to Hyland OnBase.
capabilities.label: customer-requested
acceptance: A user can upload, view and download a document of a supported type and size.
Document versions and access are tracked so an auditor can reconstruct who accessed what.

capabilities.name: Forms and Data Capture
capabilities.scope: Provide forms and structured data capture so users can submit the information the process requires with built-in validation. It delivers: BR_01 (Reduce claim-intake processing time), BR_04 (Enable direct agent claim submission), FR_07 (Agent-scoped claim visibility). It connects to Legacy ClaimsDesk Portal.
capabilities.label: customer-requested
acceptance: A form rejects incomplete or invalid submissions with a clear, field-level message.
A submitted form is stored in a structured shape a downstream process can consume.

capabilities.name: Notifications and Alerts
capabilities.scope: Provide notifications and alerts so users and administrators are informed of relevant events across the channels they use. It delivers: FR_09 (SIU flagging with automatic notification).
capabilities.label: customer-requested
acceptance: A triggering event produces a notification on every configured channel within the agreed delay.
A user can manage which notification categories they receive.

capabilities.name: Payments and Billing
capabilities.scope: Provide payments and billing so users can pay, be invoiced or reconcile charges through the platform. It delivers: BR_02 (Unified claim, policy and payment view for examiners), FR_03 (Consolidated claim timeline), FR_04 (Automated payment posting to SAP S/4HANA). It connects to Guidewire ClaimCenter, SAP S/4HANA.
capabilities.label: customer-requested
acceptance: A payment can be captured end to end and the resulting invoice matches the amount charged.
A failed or disputed payment is surfaced to the user and to finance without manual reconciliation.

capabilities.name: Self-Service Portal
capabilities.scope: Provide a self-service portal that gives users a single place to manage their account, requests and records. It delivers: FR_05 (Policyholder self-service claim status).
capabilities.label: customer-requested
acceptance: A user can complete their primary self-service task without contacting support.
The portal reflects the current state of the underlying records without a stale cache.

capabilities.name: Workflow and Approvals
capabilities.scope: Provide workflow and approvals so multi-step processes route to the right approver with a visible status at every stage. It delivers: BR_04 (Enable direct agent claim submission). It connects to SAP S/4HANA.
capabilities.label: customer-requested
acceptance: A submitted item routes to the correct approver and its status is visible to the submitter.
An approval or rejection is recorded with the approver identity and a timestamp.

capabilities.name: Core Platform Services
capabilities.scope: Provide the cross-cutting platform services - configuration, environment setup, logging and shared infrastructure - that every capability in this scope depends on. It delivers: BR_03 (Improve first-contact resolution for simple claims), BR_05 (Policyholder claim-status tracker (candidate)), FR_01 (Claim record lifecycle management), FR_08 (Seven-year claim history retention), NFR_01 (99.9% availability during business hours), NFR_02 (Sub-2-second claim search performance), NFR_03 (Registered user base of approximately 242,000), NFR_04 (Claim-data RPO/RTO targets), NFR_05 (WCAG 2.1 AA accessibility), NFR_06 (900 concurrent sessions during catastrophe events), INT_06 (Hyland OnBase document-imaging integration), SEC_01 (GDPR scope for EU-resident policyholders).
capabilities.label: assumption-to-confirm
acceptance: The shared platform services are available before any dependent capability is demonstrated.
A requirement placed here is revisited once its signals are refined so it can move to a named capability.

capabilities.name: Data Migration
capabilities.scope: Migrate existing records into the new platform with a validated mapping from each legacy field to its target. It delivers: DATA_01 (Legacy claim data migration), DATA_02 (Scanned attachment migration), DATA_04 (Migration reconciliation checks).
capabilities.label: customer-requested
acceptance: A migration dry run reconciles record counts and key fields against the source system.
Migration rejects or exceptions are reviewable rather than silently dropped.

capabilities.name: Data Quality and Reconciliation
capabilities.scope: Implement data-quality checks and reconciliation so discrepancies between systems are caught before they reach reporting. It delivers: DATA_04 (Migration reconciliation checks).
capabilities.label: customer-requested
acceptance: A scheduled reconciliation run reports discrepancies between the source and target systems.
A data-quality rule failure blocks the affected record from reaching downstream reporting.

capabilities.name: Data Retention and Archival
capabilities.scope: Apply retention and archival rules so data is kept only as long as policy and regulation require. It delivers: DATA_05 (Cold-storage archival for claims over seven years (candidate)).
capabilities.label: customer-requested
acceptance: Data past its retention period is archived or purged on the configured schedule.
An archival or purge run produces an auditable record of what was removed and when.

capabilities.name: Document and Content Data Management
capabilities.scope: Manage documents and unstructured content as first-class data, indexed so it can be searched, retrieved and governed. It delivers: DATA_02 (Scanned attachment migration). It connects to Hyland OnBase.
capabilities.label: customer-requested
acceptance: A stored document is retrievable by its metadata without a full-text scan of every file.
Document storage enforces the same access controls as the record it belongs to.

capabilities.name: Personal Data Protection
capabilities.scope: Classify and protect the personal or sensitive data the solution collects, with access limited to what each role needs. It delivers: DATA_03 (Claim and policyholder PII classification).
capabilities.label: customer-requested
acceptance: Every data field holding personal data is classified and its access is restricted by role.
A subject-access or deletion request can be fulfilled without a manual database query.

capabilities.name: API Integration Platform
capabilities.scope: Build an API-based exchange so counterpart systems can integrate through a documented, versioned interface. It delivers: INT_04 (Agent-facing claim-submission API).
capabilities.label: customer-requested
acceptance: The published API contract matches what the integrated system actually receives in production.
A breaking API change follows the agreed versioning policy instead of breaking an existing consumer.

capabilities.name: Email and SMS Gateway Integration
capabilities.scope: Integrate with an email and SMS gateway so transactional and notification messages are delivered through an auditable provider. It delivers: INT_05 (Twilio SMS/email claim notifications).
capabilities.label: customer-requested
acceptance: A triggering event produces a delivered message with a provider delivery receipt on record.
A bounced or undeliverable message is retried or flagged rather than silently dropped.

capabilities.name: ERP Integration
capabilities.scope: Integrate with the customer's ERP platform so financial and operational master data stays consistent between the two systems. It delivers: INT_02 (SAP S/4HANA payment-posting integration). It connects to SAP S/4HANA.
capabilities.label: customer-requested
acceptance: Financial or operational records posted from the platform reconcile with the ERP ledger.
A rejected ERP transaction is surfaced back to the originating user.

capabilities.name: Identity Provider Integration
capabilities.scope: Integrate with the customer's identity provider so users authenticate with their existing corporate or consumer credentials. It delivers: INT_03 (Okta SSO federation). It connects to Okta.
capabilities.label: customer-requested
acceptance: A user federates in through the configured identity provider without a separate platform password.
A deprovisioned identity-provider account loses platform access on its next sign-in attempt.

capabilities.name: Real-Time Integration Platform
capabilities.scope: Build a real-time, event-driven exchange so downstream systems receive updates as they happen rather than on a batch delay. It delivers: INT_01 (Guidewire ClaimCenter integration).
capabilities.label: customer-requested
acceptance: An event published by the platform reaches every subscriber within the agreed real-time latency budget.
A dropped or duplicate event is detected rather than silently corrupting downstream state.

capabilities.name: AI Recommendations Engine
capabilities.scope: Deliver AI-based recommendations so users are shown the next-best option based on their context and history. It delivers: FR_10 (Advisory reserve-range suggestion for examiners).
capabilities.label: customer-requested
acceptance: Recommendation relevance is measurable against a baseline through an agreed offline or online metric.
A user without sufficient history still receives a sensible default recommendation.

capabilities.name: Audit Logging and Compliance Monitoring
capabilities.scope: Implement audit logging so every access to sensitive data or privileged action can be reconstructed after the fact. It delivers: NFR_07 (Immutable seven-year audit log).
capabilities.label: customer-requested
acceptance: A privileged action is recorded with who performed it, when, and against which record.
Audit records are tamper-evident and retained for the period compliance requires.

capabilities.name: Data Encryption
capabilities.scope: Implement encryption at rest and in transit for the data classes the reviewed scope identifies as sensitive. It delivers: SEC_02 (Encryption at rest and in transit).
capabilities.label: customer-requested
acceptance: Sensitive data at rest is encrypted and the encryption keys are managed outside the application code.
Every network path carrying sensitive data uses TLS with no plaintext fallback.

capabilities.name: Multi-Factor Authentication
capabilities.scope: Implement multi-factor authentication so a compromised password alone cannot grant access to the platform. It delivers: SEC_04 (MFA for payment approval).
capabilities.label: customer-requested
acceptance: Sign-in requires a second factor for every account in the roles the reviewed scope designates.
A user can recover access through a documented, auditable process when they lose their second factor.

capabilities.name: Network Protection
capabilities.scope: Implement network protection controls so the platform's attack surface is limited to what the solution actually needs to expose. It delivers: SEC_05 (Third-party penetration testing).
capabilities.label: customer-requested
acceptance: Only the ports and services the solution needs are reachable from outside the network boundary.
A network-layer scan of the deployed environment finds no unintended public exposure.

capabilities.name: Role-Based Access Control
capabilities.scope: Implement role-based access control so each user's permissions match their responsibilities and nothing more. It delivers: SEC_03 (Role-based claim access control). It connects to Guidewire ClaimCenter.
capabilities.label: customer-requested
acceptance: A user assigned a role can perform only the actions that role is permitted.
A permission change made through role administration takes effect without a redeploy.

capabilities.name: Secrets and Credential Management
capabilities.scope: Implement secrets and credential management so API keys and service credentials are never stored in code or configuration files. It delivers: SEC_06 (Revocable scoped API credentials for agents).
capabilities.label: customer-requested
acceptance: A secrets scan of the codebase and configuration finds no hard-coded credential.
A leaked credential can be rotated without a code change or redeploy.

recommendedEnhancements.name: Observability and Operations Dashboard
recommendedEnhancements.scope: Stand up centralised logging, metrics and alerting so the availability, performance and scale targets in NFR_01, NFR_02, NFR_03, NFR_04, NFR_06 are continuously measurable rather than assumed at go-live.
recommendedEnhancements.label: recommended-enhancement
acceptance: Uptime, latency and error-rate dashboards are available to the delivery and operations teams.
A breach of an agreed threshold raises an alert within five minutes.

recommendedEnhancements.label: recommended-enhancement
acceptance: An independent accessibility audit report is produced for every customer-facing screen in scope.
Every critical and serious finding is remediated before go-live.

recommendedEnhancements.name: Security and Compliance Hardening Review
recommendedEnhancements.scope: Commission an independent penetration test and compliance review of the controls implemented for NFR_07, INT_01, INT_03, DATA_03, SEC_01, SEC_02, SEC_03, SEC_04, SEC_05, SEC_06 before production release.
recommendedEnhancements.label: recommended-enhancement
acceptance: A third-party penetration test report is delivered with no unresolved critical findings.
Compliance evidence is filed against every cited control before go-live.

recommendedEnhancements.name: Data Quality and Governance Program
recommendedEnhancements.scope: Define data-quality rules, named ownership and a reconciliation cadence for the data domains in FR_02, FR_03, FR_05, FR_06, FR_08, NFR_07, INT_06, DATA_01, DATA_02, DATA_03, DATA_04, DATA_05, SEC_02 so downstream reporting stays trustworthy.
recommendedEnhancements.label: recommended-enhancement
acceptance: Data-quality rules run on a schedule and publish a pass/fail report.
A named data owner is recorded for every data domain in scope.

summary.text: The proposed solution architecture targets Microsoft Azure and is composed of 30 components covering 25 functional capabilities. It spans the full reviewed scope; see each component’s own rationale below for its specific citations.
summary.label: ai-interpretation

components.name: Web Front End
components.service: Azure Static Web Apps with Azure Front Door
components.purpose: Serves the customer-facing web experience and delivers static assets close to users.
components.rationale: Azure Static Web Apps with Azure Front Door serves the web experience with edge caching, TLS termination and low first-byte latency worldwide. It addresses NFR_02 and NFR_05.
tradeOffs: Edge caching improves latency but requires explicit cache-invalidation on release.
A globally distributed edge adds a small recurring data-transfer cost versus single-region hosting.
securityConsiderations: Enforce HTTPS-only delivery and a strict Content-Security-Policy at the edge.
Restrict direct access to origin storage so all traffic is served through the CDN.

components.name: API Layer
components.purpose: Exposes the solution's functional capabilities as versioned, governed APIs for the front end and integrations.
components.rationale: Azure API Management centralizes authentication, throttling and request validation ahead of the application compute runtime. It addresses NFR_02, NFR_03, NFR_06 and SEC_03.
tradeOffs: A managed gateway adds a small per-request latency and cost overhead versus calling services directly.
API versioning policy must be agreed early to avoid breaking existing client integrations.
securityConsiderations: Apply request-rate throttling and payload-size limits to reduce abuse and denial-of-service exposure.
Validate and authorize every request against the identity provider before it reaches the runtime.

components.name: Application Compute Runtime
components.purpose: Hosts the backend business logic that implements the reviewed functional requirements.
components.rationale: Azure Container Apps runs the backend services with managed autoscaling so capacity tracks real traffic without manual intervention. It addresses NFR_02, NFR_03 and NFR_06.
tradeOffs: Container-based hosting requires a build/release pipeline for every deployable service.
Autoscaling limits must be tuned against real traffic before go-live to avoid cost or latency surprises.
securityConsiderations: Run containers with least-privilege service identities and no long-lived static credentials.
Scan container images for known vulnerabilities before each release.

components.name: Primary Relational Database
components.service: Azure Database for PostgreSQL - Flexible Server
components.purpose: Stores the core transactional data the application reads and writes.
components.rationale: Azure Database for PostgreSQL - Flexible Server provides managed relational storage with automated backups, patching and encryption at rest. It addresses NFR_02, NFR_03, NFR_06 and SEC_02.
tradeOffs: A managed relational engine caps vertical scale; very high write throughput may need read replicas or partitioning later.
Schema migrations must be coordinated with application deployments to avoid downtime.
securityConsiderations: Encrypt data at rest and in transit, and restrict network access to the application tier only.
Apply least-privilege database roles per service rather than a single shared credential.

components.name: Customer Identity and Access Management
components.purpose: Handles registration, sign-in, session management and multi-factor authentication for end users.
components.rationale: Microsoft Entra External ID provides managed sign-up, sign-in, SSO federation and MFA so authentication is never implemented by hand. It addresses SEC_03 and SEC_04.
tradeOffs: A managed identity provider constrains custom sign-in UX to its supported customization hooks.
Federating with an external identity provider (SSO) adds a dependency on that provider’s availability.
securityConsiderations: Enforce MFA for privileged accounts and require strong password/session policies for all users.
Log every authentication and authorization decision for audit purposes.

components.name: Monitoring
components.purpose: Tracks infrastructure and application health so incidents are detected before customers report them.
components.rationale: Azure Monitor aggregates metrics and dashboards with alerting thresholds tied to the availability and performance targets. It addresses NFR_01, NFR_04, NFR_07 and SEC_01.
tradeOffs: Alert thresholds must be tuned to avoid both alert fatigue and missed incidents.
Detailed metric retention adds a recurring storage cost proportional to system scale.
securityConsiderations: Restrict dashboard and alert access to operations and engineering roles only.

components.name: Centralized Logging
components.purpose: Centralizes application and infrastructure logs for troubleshooting and audit.
components.rationale: Azure Monitor Log Analytics aggregates structured logs from every service with a defined, policy-driven retention period. It addresses NFR_07.
tradeOffs: Centralized log retention has a direct storage cost that scales with request volume.
Log content must be scrubbed of personal or sensitive data before it is retained.
securityConsiderations: Redact personal or sensitive data from log payloads before they are written.
Restrict log access to authorized operations staff and retain an access audit trail.

components.name: CI/CD Pipeline
components.purpose: Automates build, test and release of every service into each environment.
components.rationale: Azure Pipelines runs the build/test/release pipeline consistently across development, test and production. It addresses TECH_01, TECH_02, TECH_03, CON_01, CON_02, CON_03, CON_04 and CON_05.
tradeOffs: A fully automated pipeline needs an initial investment in test coverage to be trustworthy for production releases.
securityConsiderations: Require code review and passing automated security scans before a release can be promoted.
Keep deployment credentials scoped to the pipeline identity, never to individual engineers.

components.name: Infrastructure as Code
components.purpose: Defines every environment declaratively so dev/test/prod stay reproducible and auditable.
components.rationale: Azure Resource Manager (Bicep templates) provisions and updates cloud resources declaratively, so environment drift is detected instead of accumulating silently. It addresses TECH_01, TECH_02, TECH_03, CON_01, CON_02, CON_03, CON_04 and CON_05.
tradeOffs: Declarative provisioning has a learning curve for teams used to manual console changes.
securityConsiderations: Store infrastructure state and variables in a controlled, access-audited location, never in source control in plain text.

components.name: Secrets Manager
components.purpose: Stores and rotates credentials, API keys and connection strings used by every service.
components.rationale: Azure Key Vault (secrets) centralizes credential storage with automatic rotation and fine-grained access policies. It addresses SEC_06.
tradeOffs: Every service must be updated to fetch secrets at runtime rather than reading them from local configuration.
securityConsiderations: Grant read access to a secret only to the specific service identities that need it.
Rotate credentials on a defined schedule and immediately after any suspected exposure.

components.name: Key Management
components.purpose: Manages the encryption keys that protect data at rest across storage and database services.
components.rationale: Azure Key Vault (keys, HSM-backed) issues and rotates encryption keys with a full audit trail of every key-use event. It addresses SEC_02 and SEC_06.
tradeOffs: Customer-managed keys add operational responsibility for key rotation and recovery policy.
securityConsiderations: Rotate keys on a defined schedule and restrict key administration to a small, audited group.

components.name: Backup
components.purpose: Protects stored data with policy-driven, regularly tested backups.
components.rationale: Azure Backup takes policy-driven, encrypted backups on a defined schedule with a tested restore procedure. It addresses NFR_01 and NFR_04.
tradeOffs: Backup retention has a direct storage cost that scales with data volume and retention period.
securityConsiderations: Encrypt backups at rest and test restores on a regular schedule, not only after an incident.

components.name: Network Protection
components.service: Azure Virtual Network with Private Endpoints
components.purpose: Isolates backend services on a private network so they are not directly reachable from the public internet.
components.rationale: Azure Virtual Network with Private Endpoints keeps service-to-service traffic off the public internet and restricts inbound access to approved paths only. It addresses SEC_05.
tradeOffs: Private networking adds configuration overhead when a new service or integration needs external connectivity.
securityConsiderations: Default to deny-all network rules and open only the specific paths a service requires.
Log and periodically review network access-control changes.

components.name: WAF / DDoS Protection
components.service: Azure Web Application Firewall with Azure DDoS Protection
components.purpose: Filters malicious inbound traffic and absorbs volumetric attacks at the edge, in front of the public entry point.
components.rationale: Azure Web Application Firewall with Azure DDoS Protection inspects inbound requests against managed and custom rule sets and mitigates volumetric attacks before they reach the application. It addresses SEC_05.
tradeOffs: Rule tuning is required to avoid false positives blocking legitimate traffic.
securityConsiderations: Enable managed rule sets for common web exploits and review blocked-request logs regularly.
Alert on traffic patterns consistent with a volumetric or application-layer attack.

components.name: Integration API Management
components.purpose: Publishes governed, versioned endpoints for partner and internal system integrations, separate from the product’s own front-end API.
components.rationale: Azure API Management exposes integration endpoints with independent throttling, auth and monitoring from the customer-facing API. It addresses INT_01, INT_02, INT_03, INT_04 and INT_05.
tradeOffs: Running a second managed API surface adds a small recurring cost versus reusing the front-end API layer.
securityConsiderations: Require mutual authentication (API key or mTLS) for every partner system calling this surface.

components.name: Integration Service
components.purpose: Coordinates data exchange with the external systems identified in the reviewed scope.
components.rationale: Azure Logic Apps provides managed connectors, retry and error-handling policy for each external-system integration. It addresses INT_01, INT_02, INT_03, INT_04 and INT_05.
tradeOffs: Each new external system requires its own connector configuration, credential and monitoring setup.
securityConsiderations: Store integration credentials in the secrets manager and scope them per external system.

components.name: Message Queue
components.purpose: Decouples integration producers and consumers so a slow or unavailable external system does not block the application.
components.rationale: Azure Service Bus (queues) buffers integration messages with dead-letter handling so failed deliveries are retried rather than lost. It addresses INT_01, INT_02, INT_03, INT_04 and INT_05.
tradeOffs: Asynchronous delivery means consumers must tolerate eventual, not immediate, consistency.
securityConsiderations: Encrypt messages in transit and at rest, and restrict queue access to the integration service identity.

components.name: Event Bus
components.purpose: Routes near-real-time events between the application and external systems that require immediate synchronization.
components.rationale: Azure Event Grid routes schema-validated events to subscribers with sub-second delivery for real-time synchronization needs. It addresses INT_01.
tradeOffs: Event-driven synchronization requires each consumer to handle duplicate or out-of-order delivery.
securityConsiderations: Restrict event publication to authenticated service identities and validate event schemas at the bus.

components.name: Data Warehouse
components.purpose: Provides a column-oriented analytical store for cross-domain reporting and analysis.
components.rationale: Azure Synapse Analytics (dedicated SQL pool) holds curated, query-optimized data separate from transactional load so reporting never competes with production traffic. It addresses FR_02, FR_06 and DATA_04.
tradeOffs: A separate analytical store adds pipeline latency between an event occurring and it being reportable.
securityConsiderations: Apply row/column-level access controls so analysts see only the data domains they are authorized for.

components.name: ETL Pipeline
components.purpose: Moves and transforms data from source systems into the analytical store or between domains.
components.rationale: Azure Data Factory runs scheduled extraction and transformation jobs with data-quality checks before data lands downstream. It addresses FR_03, DATA_01, DATA_02 and DATA_04.
tradeOffs: Pipeline failures require monitoring and a defined re-run/backfill procedure to avoid silent data gaps.
securityConsiderations: Mask or tokenize sensitive fields during transformation before data reaches lower-trust environments.

components.name: Object Storage
components.purpose: Stores documents and other unstructured content referenced by the application.
components.rationale: Azure Blob Storage stores unstructured content durably with lifecycle policies and encryption at rest. It addresses FR_02, FR_05, INT_06 and DATA_02.
tradeOffs: Large unstructured content volumes need an explicit lifecycle/retention policy to control storage cost.
securityConsiderations: Generate time-limited access URLs rather than exposing storage buckets/containers directly.

components.name: BI / Reporting
components.purpose: Delivers self-service dashboards and reports to business stakeholders over the warehouse.
components.rationale: Power BI provides governed, self-service dashboards over curated warehouse data. It addresses FR_02, FR_06 and DATA_04.
tradeOffs: Self-service reporting requires a governed semantic layer to prevent conflicting metric definitions.
securityConsiderations: Scope dashboard access by role so stakeholders see only their authorized data domains.

components.name: LLM Platform
components.service: Azure OpenAI in Azure AI Foundry
components.purpose: Provides managed access to foundation models for the AI use cases identified in the reviewed scope.
components.rationale: Azure OpenAI in Azure AI Foundry gives managed, guardrailed access to foundation models so AI functionality is not built on an unmanaged model endpoint. It addresses FR_10.
tradeOffs: Model responses are probabilistic; outputs affecting decisions need a human-review step (see AI solution approach).
securityConsiderations: Apply content-safety guardrails and never send unmasked personal data in a prompt without a documented basis.

components.name: ML Platform
components.purpose: Trains, deploys and monitors the predictive models behind forecasting, anomaly detection or recommendation use cases.
components.rationale: Azure Machine Learning trains and serves predictive models with drift monitoring, distinct from the generative LLM platform. It addresses FR_10.
tradeOffs: Predictive models need a labeled training dataset and ongoing retraining as behavior/data patterns shift.

The driving requirement is Low-priority and not yet fully defined; a simple rules-based heuristic instead of a trained model until enough labeled data exists would be sufficient until it is confirmed, rather than committing to this component now.
securityConsiderations: Monitor for model drift and bias, and restrict retraining access to the ML engineering team.

components.name: High Availability & Autoscaling
components.service: Zone-redundant Azure Container Apps environment with KEDA scale rules
components.purpose: Distributes traffic and compute capacity across multiple availability zones to sustain the required uptime.
components.rationale: Zone-redundant Azure Container Apps environment with KEDA scale rules spreads compute across multiple availability zones with automatic failover and load-based scaling. It addresses NFR_01 and NFR_04.
tradeOffs: Multi-AZ deployment increases baseline infrastructure cost versus a single-instance deployment.
securityConsiderations: Ensure failover paths are exercised in a game-day/DR test, not only documented.

components.name: Disaster Recovery / Multi-Region
components.service: Azure Database for PostgreSQL cross-region read replica with geo-redundant backup (paired region)
components.purpose: Provides a cross-region recovery path so the service can be restored after a regional outage.
components.rationale: Azure Database for PostgreSQL cross-region read replica with geo-redundant backup (paired region) replicates critical data and configuration to a secondary region with a documented recovery time/point objective. It addresses NFR_01 and NFR_04.
tradeOffs: A warm or hot standby region roughly doubles the infrastructure cost of the protected components.
securityConsiderations: Keep the secondary region’s access controls and encryption configuration in parity with primary.

components.name: Cache
components.purpose: Reduces database load and read latency for frequently accessed data under high concurrent usage.
components.rationale: Azure Cache for Redis serves hot read paths from memory so the relational database is not the scaling bottleneck under peak load. It addresses NFR_02, NFR_03 and NFR_06.
tradeOffs: Cached data can briefly go stale after a write; time-to-live and invalidation rules must be defined per data type.
securityConsiderations: Encrypt cache traffic and avoid caching personal data beyond the minimum required time-to-live.

components.name: Search Service
components.purpose: Provides fast, relevant search and discovery over application content.
components.rationale: Azure AI Search indexes application content for fast, relevance-ranked search rather than relying on database queries. It addresses NFR_02.

integrations.name: Guidewire ClaimCenter integration
integrations.authentication: OAuth 2.0 client credentials grant on the event broker connection
integrations.errorHandling: Every event published to Guidewire ClaimCenter carries an idempotency key so a redelivered or duplicated event is never applied twice, and an event that cannot be processed is moved to a dead-letter queue rather than blocking the stream.
integrations.retry: Exponential backoff starting at 1 second and doubling to a 5-attempt ceiling for calls to Guidewire ClaimCenter, after which the call is routed to the dead-letter queue instead of retried forever.
integrations.monitoring: Publish/consume lag and dead-letter queue depth for the Guidewire ClaimCenter event stream are tracked in Azure Monitor, Azure Monitor Log Analytics, with an alert routed to the delivery team when lag or queue depth crosses its threshold.
integrations.dataSync: Guidewire ClaimCenter is treated as the system of record for the fields it owns; conflicting updates are resolved by last-writer-wins on the record's own timestamp, and a daily reconciliation job compares record counts between Guidewire ClaimCenter and the platform to surface drift instead of assuming the sync is complete.

frameworks.name: Custom orchestration
frameworks.rationale: The reviewed AI scope (FR_10) is a single linear pipeline (parse/score, then a confidence-threshold branch); a lightweight custom orchestrator calling the model SDK directly delivers that without the operational overhead of a graph-based agent framework built for multi-step, looping workflows it does not need.

frameworks.rationale: The stated technology preference (TECH_03) is .NET/Azure; Semantic Kernel is Microsoft's own orchestration SDK for that stack and integrates directly with Azure AI Foundry model deployments without a cross-language bridge.
alternatives: LangChain/LangGraph (Python/TypeScript-first; usable from .NET only through an extra service boundary the reviewed stack does not call for).

frameworks.rationale: Hosting the model(s) for FR_10 on Azure OpenAI in Azure AI Foundry, Azure Machine Learning keeps inference inside the Microsoft Azure account boundary already used for the rest of the solution, avoiding a separate vendor contract, network egress path and access-control model to operate.
alternatives: A self-hosted open-weight model on Kubernetes/GPU nodes (higher operational overhead; only justified by a strict data-residency or cost-at-scale constraint the reviewed scope does not state).

suggestion.explanation: The estimate inputs for ClaimsDesk Modernization Program are organised into 7 workstreams and 33 scope drivers across the build phases Experience and Core Platform, Data and Integration and AI Capabilities; Discovery and Architecture, Testing and Hardening, and Deployment and Handover are added as configurable overheads. Each driver cites the reviewed requirements, capabilities, architecture components, integrations or AI use cases that justify it, and its complexity is derived from the facts named in its rationale. A capability whose reviewed requirements are all already priced by AI use-case, integration or data drivers is priced once, in those more specific workstreams, never twice; two capabilities built from the same requirements are combined into one driver. The main complexity hotspots are Forms and Data Capture (DRV_03), Payments and Billing (DRV_05), Core Platform Services (DRV_08), Cloud platform foundation and environments (DRV_15), Performance and scalability hardening (DRV_17), SAP S/4HANA payment-posting integration (DRV_22), Okta SSO federation (DRV_23), Twilio SMS/email claim notifications (DRV_25), Hyland OnBase document-imaging integration (DRV_26), Legacy ClaimsDesk Portal (parallel-run cutover) (DRV_27) and Migration reconciliation checks (DRV_31). Security and compliance work is delivered through the named security capability in the functional scope, so no separate generic security workstream is planned; that would price the same controls twice. Only complexity levels are suggested here: effort, timeline and ROM values are calculated from the base-effort table, role mix, day rates, contingency and team size in the estimation configuration.

rules.name: Driver effort
rules.formula: driver days = baseEffort[driver type][complexity]; complexity = reviewer override ?? AI suggestion
rules.description: Each scope driver is sized from the editable base-effort table. The AI only suggests the complexity level; a reviewer override replaces it and is marked user-set. A driver without a base-effort value contributes no days, is reported as a blocked scope driver and blocks the cost of its workstream and the ROM.

rules.name: Workstream base effort and complexity
rules.formula: base days = sum(driver days); complexity = round(sum(level x driver days) / sum(driver days)), Low = 1 ... Very High = 4
rules.description: A workstream is the sum of its drivers. Its complexity is the effort-weighted average of the driver complexity levels.

rules.name: Environment uplift
rules.formula: infrastructure days x (1 + max(0, environments - baselineEnvironments) x extraEnvironmentPct / 100)
rules.description: Environments beyond the baseline add effort to infrastructure drivers only. When the number of environments is unknown, no uplift is applied, the input is listed as missing and confidence is reduced.

rules.name: Productivity factor
rules.formula: likely days = round((non-infrastructure days + uplifted infrastructure days) x productivityFactor)
rules.description: The productivity assumption scales all build effort (below 1 is faster than baseline). Likely effort is rounded to whole days.

rules.name: Overhead phases
rules.formula: phase days = round(total likely build days x pctOfBuild / 100)
rules.description: Discovery and Architecture, Testing and Hardening, and Deployment and Handover are sized as configurable percentages of the adjusted build effort and staffed with the overhead role mix.

rules.name: Workstream confidence
rules.formula: High -> Medium (Very High driver, related open gap or question, outstanding delivery dependency, missing planning input) -> Low (critical unresolved gap or question on an affected input, or a blocked calculation)
rules.description: Inputs map to workstreams by driver type: integration readiness -> integration, data volume -> data, AI data availability -> AI, expected users / environments / target regions -> infrastructure, compliance scope -> security, delivery deadline -> timeline. Every reduction is listed as a confidence limitation. Overhead phases inherit the overall confidence.

rules.name: Overall confidence
rules.formula: Low if any calculation is blocked, Low-confidence workstreams hold >= 30% of build effort, or 4 or more distinct estimation inputs are missing; Medium if any workstream is below High or any input is missing; else High
rules.description: The overall level is weighted by effort so that one small uncertain workstream does not dominate, while blocked calculations and a largely unspecified engagement always do.

rules.name: Effort range
rules.formula: low = round(likely x (1 - lowPct / 100)); high = round(likely x (1 + highPct / 100))
rules.description: The range width comes from the confidence-spread table, so lower confidence widens the range instead of presenting unsupported precision. Totals are the sums of the workstream ranges.

rules.name: Role allocation
rules.formula: role days = likely days x sum(driver-type days x role mix share) / sum(driver-type days), in tenths of a day (largest remainder)
rules.description: Likely effort is split across roles with the role mix of each driver type, weighted by that type's days. Role days always add up exactly to the likely effort.

rules.name: Workstream cost
rules.formula: cost = sum(role days x role day rate); range = cost x (1 - lowPct / 100) .. cost x (1 + highPct / 100)
rules.description: A role with allocated days but no day rate, effort without a role mix, or a driver without base effort blocks the workstream cost and the ROM totals. No default rate is ever substituted.

rules.name: ROM commercials
rules.formula: subtotal = roundToUnit(sum(workstream cost)); contingency = roundToUnit(subtotal x contingencyPct / 100); ROM = subtotal + contingency
rules.description: Low, likely and high values are each rounded to the configured rounding unit and reported in the configured currency.

rules.name: Timeline
rules.formula: capacity = teamSize x workingDaysPerWeek; weeks = ceil(effort / capacity); build window = ceil(sum(build phase effort) / capacity)
rules.description: Discovery runs first; the build phases run concurrently and share the team; Testing and Hardening may overlap the last 25% of the build window but always keeps at least one week after it; Deployment and Handover runs last. The range applies the timeline confidence spread, rounded up to whole weeks.

rules.name: Deadline assessment
rules.formula: compare likely and high timeline weeks with deliveryDeadlineWeeks; required team = smallest team size whose likely timeline <= deadline
rules.description: When no deadline is configured the assessment says so, the deadline is listed as a missing input and timeline confidence is reduced.

rules.name: Missing inputs
rules.formula: missing planning input -> confidence reduced; missing day rate, role mix or base effort -> calculation blocked
rules.description: Each missing input names the affected workstreams or estimate components, the related scope items and how to resolve it. An input held open by a gap or question is never dropped: without a workstream of its driver type it affects the workstreams that share requirements with the open item, otherwise the overall estimate.

rules.name: Historical references
rules.description: Illustrative historical delivery references (sample data, not actual Topcoder records) are displayed for context only and are never an input to any rule above.

result.deadlineAssessment: The 46-week deadline is achievable: even the high end of the timeline range (28 weeks) fits, against a likely 21 weeks. The configured team of 6 is sufficient; the smallest average team that still meets the deadline at the likely effort is 3.
result.explanation: The estimate inputs for ClaimsDesk Modernization Program are organised into 7 workstreams and 33 scope drivers across the build phases Experience and Core Platform, Data and Integration and AI Capabilities; Discovery and Architecture, Testing and Hardening, and Deployment and Handover are added as configurable overheads. Each driver cites the reviewed requirements, capabilities, architecture components, integrations or AI use cases that justify it, and its complexity is derived from the facts named in its rationale. A capability whose reviewed requirements are all already priced by AI use-case, integration or data drivers is priced once, in those more specific workstreams, never twice; two capabilities built from the same requirements are combined into one driver. The main complexity hotspots are Forms and Data Capture (DRV_03), Payments and Billing (DRV_05), Core Platform Services (DRV_08), Cloud platform foundation and environments (DRV_15), Performance and scalability hardening (DRV_17), SAP S/4HANA payment-posting integration (DRV_22), Okta SSO federation (DRV_23), Twilio SMS/email claim notifications (DRV_25), Hyland OnBase document-imaging integration (DRV_26), Legacy ClaimsDesk Portal (parallel-run cutover) (DRV_27) and Migration reconciliation checks (DRV_31). Security and compliance work is delivered through the named security capability in the functional scope, so no separate generic security workstream is planned; that would price the same controls twice. Only complexity levels are suggested here: effort, timeline and ROM values are calculated from the base-effort table, role mix, day rates, contingency and team size in the estimation configuration. Calculated effort is 572 to 885 person-days (likely 675) over 18 to 28 weeks (likely 21) with Medium overall confidence. The ROM commercial range is 538,000 USD to 828,000 USD (likely 634,000 USD) including 15% contingency. Every figure is produced by the documented calculation rules CR_01 to CR_15 from the visible drivers and configuration; none is generated by the AI.

executiveSummary:
This scoping package covers Meridian Assurance Group's ClaimsDesk Modernization Program, grounded in 5 business objectives, 10 functional requirements and 7 non-functional requirements reviewed from the customer's own requirements text, alongside 6 integrations and 6 security or compliance requirements that shape the proposed solution.

Cloud platform: Microsoft Azure; Requirement coverage: 100%; Effort estimate: 572 to 885 person-days (likely 675); Timeline: 18 to 28 weeks; ROM commercial range: 538,000 USD to 828,000 USD (likely 634,000 USD); Estimate confidence: Medium; Open questions: 3. 3 clarification questions remain open and should be resolved before this package is finalised. This summary and the estimates that follow are an AI-assisted planning output and require review and validation by qualified sales, architecture, delivery, security and commercial stakeholders before being shared with Meridian Assurance Group.
